newsitem.title: UK: Metals end steadier, LME marks time in PM.
newsitem.headline: Metals end steadier, LME marks time in PM.

text.p: Base metal prices stayed close to early highs during Tuesday afternoon LME trading, finishing a stable session steadier across the board.
Traders said the complex lacked the follow through to extend the current mini-technical bounce, and opted instead to consolidate gains. Conditions were not particularly active.
"Copper got to $2,280, but didn't really fancy going much further. I still think these rallies are there to be sold into," one said.
Also, there is the lingering perception that investment funds, who may be short already, are waiting to sell into higher levels.

Nevertheless, copper seems to be well supported by technicals, with good chart buying likely around $2,250. Additionally, the market is cautious ahead of a strike vote later on Tuesday at Escondida - the world's largest copper mine.
Three months prices peaked at $2,287 a tonne before closing at $2,281, up $24 from Monday. The cash/threes backwardation was at $35/37, little changed from yesterday.
By comparison, aluminium struggled to make an impression on the upside, and traded in a narrow, albeit steadier range. Last business was at $1,555 a tonne, up just $6 from the previous kerb.
Nickel prices remained firmer during the afternoon, without breaching $7,400, closing at $7,390, up $150 a tonne from yesterday.
Traders said the market ignored the 1,872-tonne increase in stocks, which was a surprising briquettes delivery, and built on recent physical strength.
There has been goood widespread interest from Europe, the Far East, and North America, which tempered Monday's fund sales, they said.
Both lead and zinc remained steadier towards the close, with the latter metal aided by another inventory decline.
Zinc closed at $1,259, up $6 from Monday, while lead concluded at $645, a $13 gain, with the market continuing to correct from recent 18-month lows.
Tin reversed direction during laregly routine afternoon trading, and erased earlier losses to close at $5,760, up just $10 from yesterday.
Alloy was quiet, and finished at a little-changed $1,450/55 a tonne.
